newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares ease, could decline further.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares ease, could decline further.

text.p: Slovenian shares eased 1.44 percent on Friday to end the week 4.2 percent lower.

Market participants said the index could fall further in the next week as investors moved their interest to shares of newly privatised companies, of which only food producer Kolinska was included in the main SBI index.
"Investors shifted their interest to newly privatised companies and actively trade with shares of those that are listed as well as those that aren't," one trader said.
* The seven-share SBI index fell 13.77 points to 941.04.
* 11 shares fell and four rose, while eight were untraded.
* Turnover rose to 68.6 million tolars from 53 million.
* Financial consultancy Dadas had the highest turnover, falling 8.24 percent to 27,289 tolars on volume of 462 shares for total turnover of 12.6 million tolars.
* Financial consultancy Primofin was the leading decliner. Its shares fell 9.75 percent to 19,649 on volume of 54 shares for total turnover of 1.1 million tolars.

* Pharmaceutical trading company Salus was the top gainer, rising 6.61 percent to 14,479 on volume of 610 shares for total turnover of 8.8 million tolars. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
